Promise Resolve Behavior

withCorePromiseBehavior is a resolve behavior that normalizes promise-backed state inputs by invoking a deferred factory and resolving its resulting value for downstream pipeline processing.

This behavior operates exclusively in the Resolve stage. It affects how an incoming value is resolved, never when it enters the pipeline or how it is later processed. No state mutation, derivation, or policy logic occurs as part of promise resolution.

State updates are submitted through the FeatureCell APIs replaceState and mergeState. These APIs admit deferred factories that produce promises, which are resolved by the Resolve stage before downstream pipeline execution begins.

withCorePromiseBehavior participates only when a DeferredFactory<T> input is supplied. During pipeline execution, the deferred factory is invoked, the returned promise is awaited, and the resolved value is forwarded as a normalized upstream value.

Promise rejections are captured, normalized into pipeline errors, and propagated to downstream stages in a deterministic and isolated manner.

Note

Why DeferredFactory? Promises are eager by nature: once created, they begin executing immediately and may resolve or reject outside of the pipeline lifecycle. Passing a raw promise as state input would allow resolution to occur before the Resolve stage executes, potentially producing out-of-order updates, false state snapshots, or untracked errors.

Note

The DeferredFactory<T> wrapper ensures that promise execution is deferred until the Resolve stage explicitly invokes it. This guarantees that the promise is resolved inside pipeline execution, under orchestration control, with proper lifecycle binding, error normalization, and deterministic state emission.

Diagrams
Configuration

withCorePromiseBehavior requires no explicit configuration parameters. It participates automatically when a state update is supplied via replaceState or mergeState with a DeferredFactory<T> input.

The behavior is installed by default as part of the Resolve stage and activates conditionally based on the resolved input type. When a deferred factory is detected, the Resolve stage invokes the factory during pipeline execution and awaits the resulting promise before downstream processing begins.

Promise resolution is fully scoped to a single pipeline execution. The deferred factory is invoked exactly once per update, and the resolved value—or normalized error—is forwarded downstream. No subscriptions, timers, or persistent resources are retained beyond the resolution boundary.

Examples

withCorePromiseBehavior participates automatically when a DeferredFactory<T> is supplied via replaceState or mergeState. No explicit configuration is required during FeatureCell initialization.

In the examples below, a FeatureCell is initialized normally. After initialization, a promise-backed state update is submitted using replaceState. The Resolve stage invokes the deferred factory, awaits the promise, and forwards the resolved value for downstream pipeline processing.

Example 1: Resolve a Promise-Based State Update

{{`@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();

    const deferredEmployees = {
      value: () =>
        Promise.resolve([
          { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
          { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
        ])
    };

    // Submit a promise-based state update
    this.vault.replaceState(deferredEmployees);
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  }
);

employeeCell.initialize();

const deferredEmployees = {
  value: () =>
    Promise.resolve([
      { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
    ])
};

// Submit a promise-based state update
employeeCell.replaceState(deferredEmployees);`}}
